guide.p: The grammar criterion rewards both range (using varied, complex structures) and accuracy (how many sentences are free from errors). At Band 7 and above, most sentences should be error-free. The errors below are the most frequent in IELTS writing.

bullets: ✗ informations, advices, researches, equipments, knowledges → ✓ information, advice, research, equipment, knowledge
✗ a useful advice → ✓ a useful piece of advice / useful advice
✗ many evidence → ✓ much evidence / a lot of evidence
✗ Government should invest in education. → ✓ The government should invest in education.
✗ The education is important for the children. → ✓ Education is important for children. (general meaning, no 'the')
✗ In the 2010 → ✓ In 2010. But: in the 1990s, in the following year.
✗ The number of students have increased. → ✓ The number of students has increased.
✗ A number of student has complained. → ✓ A number of students have complained.
✗ Everyone have a phone. → ✓ Everyone has a phone.
✗ One of the reasons are cost. → ✓ One of the reasons is cost.
Fragment: ✗ Because cities are crowded. → ✓ Many people cycle because cities are crowded.
Comma splice: ✗ Prices rose, people bought less. → ✓ Prices rose, so people bought less. / Prices rose; as a result, people bought less.
'However' needs a full stop or semicolon before it when it joins two sentences: ✓ Cars are convenient. However, they pollute.
✗ an increase of sales → ✓ an increase in sales; ✓ an increase of 10%
✗ the amount of people → ✓ the number of people (countable); ✓ the amount of water (uncountable)
✗ It was increased sharply. → ✓ It increased sharply. (rise, fall, increase are not passive here)
Keep tenses consistent: past simple for finished years; past perfect with 'by': 'By 2010 it had doubled.'
✗ more higher, more easier → ✓ higher, easier
✗ the most cheapest → ✓ the cheapest
✗ economical growth → ✓ economic growth (economical = saving money)
✗ It is benefit for society. → ✓ It is beneficial to society. / It benefits society.
✓ affect something (verb, no preposition) / have an effect on something
✓ responsible for, interested in, depend on, focus on, discuss something (not 'discuss about')
✓ according to the chart (not 'according to me' — use 'in my opinion')

guide.tip: Keep a personal list of the errors you make most often and check your essay for those first in the last 3 minutes.
